taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. On that date, Pacific Time will be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Also on that date, Madrid will have returned to standard time, which is Central European Time (CET), or UTC+1. This means Madrid is 8 hours ahead of the contest's deadline time. Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on Friday means the deadline for you is on the following Saturday morning.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM in Los Angeles. On that date, Los Angeles will be on Pacific Standard Time (UTC-8) and Madrid will be on Central European Time (UTC+1). This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles. Adding 9 hours to 10:00 AM gives you 7:00 PM (19:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts at 18:00 on Saturday, October 24, 2026, and lasts 48 hours. This period includes the end of Daylight Saving Time in Spain, which occurs on Sunday, October 25, 2026, when the clocks go back one hour. Adding 48 hours to the start time would normally result in Monday at 18:00, but because the clocks "fall back," the end time will be one hour earlier.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Of course. Let's calculate that for you.

The contest starts at 10:00 AM on October 26, 2026, in the Pacific Time zone (PT). On that date, this will be Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is 7 hours behind UTC (UTC-7). The start time is therefore 17:00 UTC.

The submission deadline is exactly 72 hours (3 full days) later, which is October 29, 2026, at 17:00 UTC.

On that date, Madrid, Spain, will be on Central European Time (CET), which is 1 hour ahead of UTC (UTC+1). Converting the deadline to your local time means adding one hour to the UTC time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The submission deadline is October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET. On this date, the ET zone is on Daylight Saving Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. In Madrid, European Summer Time will have already ended, so your local time will be Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1. This makes Madrid 5 hours ahead of the ET zone.

The deadline in your local time is 04:59 on November 1, 2026. The results are announced 36 hours after that. Adding 36 hours (one full day and 12 hours) to 04:59 on November 1 brings us to 16:59 on November 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The provided Unix timestamp corresponds to a specific moment globally. Your local time zone, Japan Standard Time (JST), is 9 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). By converting the timestamp to UTC and then adding 9 hours, we find the deadline in your local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-16 02:39

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in UTC (indicated by the "Z"). Madrid, Spain, is on Central European Time.

On October 25, 2026, which is the last Sunday of the month, Daylight Saving Time ends. Clocks in Madrid will turn back one hour at 3:00 AM local time. This change happens at 01:00 UTC. Since the deadline of 02:30 UTC is *after* this change, Madrid will be on standard time (CET), which is 1 hour ahead of UTC (UTC+1). Therefore, the deadline is at 3:30 AM your local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25th. On that date, Pacific Time will be PDT (UTC-7) as the US has not yet ended Daylight Saving. Spain, however, ends its Daylight Saving on that very day, meaning Madrid will be on standard time, CET (UTC+1). This makes Madrid 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time. Therefore, 11:59 PM on Sunday, October 25th in Pacific Time will be 7:59 AM on Monday, October 26th in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, daylight saving time in the United States ends on Sunday, November 1st. On that day, at 12:00 noon, the US East Coast will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5. Your local time in Lima, Peru (PET) is also UTC-5 year-round. Therefore, the deadline is at the same time for you.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" means the moment the date ends everywhere on Earth. This is equivalent to 00:00 on January 1, 2027, in the last possible time zone, which is UTC-12. To find your deadline, we convert this to your local time in Tokyo (Japan Standard Time, UTC+9). The time difference between UTC-12 and UTC+9 is 21 hours. Therefore, your deadline is 21 hours *after* 00:00 on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 5, 2026, Sydney will be on Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11) and New York will also be on Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4). This makes Sydney 15 hours ahead of New York. To find the deadline in your local New York time, you need to subtract 15 hours from the Sydney time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
